For y=x+gF(x), sigmoid g∈(0,1) bounds the multiplier, not the residual magnitude: ||gF(x)||/||x|| can remain arbitrarily large. LayerNorm also permits scale growth through learned γ and β; normalization before an unconstrained output projection cannot bound that projection’s output. [Layer Normalization](https://arxiv.org/abs/1607.06450) defines these affine parameters. Thus gate values alone are insufficient diagnostics; measure the actual residual/backbone norm ratio.

Near-identity initialization has empirical support: [GTrXL](https://proceedings.mlr.press/v119/parisotto20a.html) uses gate biases favoring identity, while [ReZero](https://arxiv.org/abs/2003.04887) initializes an unconstrained residual scalar at zero. Algebraically, for g=σ(a), branch gradients scale with g and gate-logit gradients with g(1−g)F(x): strongly negative logits suppress both branch learning and gate movement; large branch activations can still amplify gate gradients. Reproducible sigmoid initialization sets a=log(g₀/(1−g₀)); zero logits produce g₀=0.5, not a near-zero gate. ReZero avoids sigmoid saturation, although branch parameter gradients initially vanish when its scalar is exactly zero.

A derived construction giving an explicit per-token relative bound is r=cσ(a)||x||₂·v/(||v||₂+ε), y=x+r, with fixed c and ε>0. Then ||r||₂≤c||x||₂, regardless of branch scale; apply this after all branch projections, affine normalization, and dropout. Affine-free LayerNorm alone bounds absolute branch norm by √d, but does not bound it relative to a small backbone vector. Record c, g₀, ε, normalization placement, and measured norm ratios; these are engineering deductions, not reported recommendation benchmarks.
